subject: Post-call: Nebula inference qualification & next test matrix
messages:
From: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>
To: Oliver Grant <oliver@nebulaanalytics.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 19 Jan 2027 14:03:00 -0800
Subject: Post-call recap + proposed test matrix

Thanks again for the call earlier, Oliver — good to learn more about Nebula's document ingestion pipeline and the two inference paths you're evaluating (hyperscaler-managed endpoints vs self-hosted). Quick recap and suggested next steps below so we all have a single checklist.

Summary (what we heard)
- Primary goal: replace legacy on-prem LLMs with a predictable, lower-cost inference layer that supports 10–50 QPS for RAG and extraction use cases.
- Key concerns: hallucination rates on long-context prompts, tail latency (p95), throughput under mixed small/long requests, and procurement constraints (SLA + data residency).
- Benchmarks you care about: hallucination rate on our probe set, mean token latency, and predicted monthly cost at 10k tokens/user/month.

Proposed evaluation matrix (short list of tests we can run this week)
1) Quality sweep (prompt suite): run the attached probe_prompts_20270119.csv across: Redwood-opt-tuned, Redwood-quant, Hyperscaler-s1. Capture: top-1 correctness, hallucination flags, and confidence calibration.
2) Hallucination stress: 10% adversarial prompts from your legal/claims docs to measure hallucination rate and failure modes.
3) Latency/throughput: mixed workload (40% short, 60% long) for 1k concurrent requests (steady-state) -> P50/P95/P99 and token/sec.
4) Cost projection: run simulated load for 1M tokens/day to estimate per-1k-token cost across variants.

Deliverables & timeline
- Redwood provides: probe results CSV, short playbook showing where behaviors diverge, and a 2-page one-pager summarizing differentiators (by Fri 2027-01-22).
- Nebula provides: sample doc subset (anonymized) and 4–6 legal prompts flagged by your team by Thu 2027-01-21.

Attachments referenced: [Attachment: probe_prompts_20270119.csv (CSV)] [Attachment: redwood-vs-hyperscaler-quicksheet.pdf (PDF)]

Immediate asks
- Oliver: confirm you can share the anonymized doc subset and whether procurement should be looped now or after the initial results.
- Ben/Laura: can you confirm the initial pricing band I'll include in the 1-pager (we discussed a mid-market reserved SKU + burst)?

Thanks — I'll kick off the test harness once we have the sample docs.

—
Tessa Morgan
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Tessa — thanks for the clear summary. We can share an anonymized doc subset; procurement wants to see a short SLA note before we run anything on our side. Two quick Qs:

1) Can you include the exact prompt strings you'll run (so we can quickly sanity-check for PII)?
2) For the hallucination stress test, can we cap that to the 5 highest-risk legal prompts first?

We're aiming for a decision by the end of Feb — happy to run the test set this week if you can provide the one-pager and a privacy/SLA bullet list. Looping procurement separately (procurement@nebulaanalytics.com) for visibility.

Oliver — glad to be on the thread. Two commercial items to make progress:

1) Pricing band: for the initial POC we can offer a month-1 evaluation credit + a capped reserved instance rate. I'll drop numbers into the one-pager that Tessa is preparing.

Oliver / procurement team — quick status update and mutually agreed action items after internal sync with SEs:

What Redwood will deliver by Fri 2027-01-29
- Full probe run results (CSV) with per-prompt judgments and hallucination markers.
- Shortplaybook.pdf: explanation of divergence points and recommended fallbacks (e.g., quantized variant if cost > target; model routing rule example).
- A one-page SLA/privacy bullet list that covers: data handling (anonymized docs only), retention window (30 days), and audit log availability.

Mutual action plan (MAP) — tentative timeline
- 2027-01-25: Nebula shares anonymized doc subset + 5 legal prompts (requested).
- 2027-01-26 to 2027-01-28: Redwood runs probe suite and latency sweep.
- 2027-01-29: Redwood delivers results + one-pager + pricing band.
- 2027-02-02: Joint sync to review results and next steps (decision milestone).

Evaluation metrics we'll provide (so procurement knows what to expect)
- Hallucination rate (per 1k prompts) with examples flagged.
- Correctness (top-1) vs gold labels for extraction tasks.
- Latency: P50/P95/P99 token-based measurements and end-to-end response times.
- Failure modes: percentage of requests returning low-confidence or server errors.
- Cost projection: monthly cost at your estimated QPS across variants.

Attachments: [Attachment: mutual-action-plan-NEB-4891.xlsx (XLSX)]

Next asks for Nebula
1) Upload anonymized doc subset to the Drive link here: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3cNEB-qual by EOD 2027-01-25.
2) Confirm procurement contact for the SLA doc (I cc'd procurement, please advise if another contact is needed).

If that timeline works I'll mark the MAP in HubSpot and kick off the run tonight (we'll rotate keys and use a redacted environment).

Thanks — looking forward to the results.

—

Account Executive, Redwood Inference
